title: On Leaning the ladder against the wall
subtitle: 工程建造 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 工程建造（科学与技术·工程与建造）
meta: 主题语境：工程建造（科学与技术·工程与建造）　|　核心词汇：lean　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 lean 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1988 the musician ① leaned the ladder against the wall before dawn, and every listener in the hall said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three nights on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the musician ② leans the ladder against the wall in public without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ lean the ladder against the wall at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ leaned the ladder against the wall before — a line in the programme for December 1982 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Leaning the ladder against the wall before dawn, the musician said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the score at the far piano, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ lean to one side after the storm in public, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Lean to one side after the storm at once and never mention it again.

By 1995 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the programme, and a new listener from the next hall ⑧ leans to one side after the storm before dawn every night without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the piano, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ leaned the ladder against the wall again when nobody else would.

⑩ To lean the ladder against the wall, my mother said in 2000, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the hall remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the hall forgets, somebody leans the ladder against the wall in public again and somebody must lean the ladder against the wall before dawn all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 倚靠（一般过去式 leaned the ladder against the wall：1988 年乐师头一回这样做，天没亮就）
B. v. 倚靠（一般现在 leans the ladder against the wall：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 倚靠（不定式 to lean the ladder against the wall：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 倚靠（过去完成时 had leaned the ladder against the wall：1982 年十二月的节目单上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 倚靠（动名词 leaning the ladder against the wall 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 倾斜（lean to one side after the storm：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去倾斜风暴过后歪向一边）
G. v. 倾斜（lean to one side after the storm：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 倚靠（后段两处：新来的听客照例 leans to one side after the storm，而母亲又一次 leaned the ladder against the wall）

answers.why: lean 意为“倚靠”，1988 年乐师天没亮就倚靠把梯子靠在墙上，那是音乐厅里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 leaned。
lean 意为“倚靠”，自那以后乐师当着众人面把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 leans。
lean 意为“倚靠”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯倚靠把梯子靠在墙上”，此处为不定式 to lean the ladder against the wall。
lean 意为“倚靠”，节目单里 十二月 那行字说明早在 1995 年之前就有人倚靠过，故用过去完成时 had leaned。
lean 意为“倚靠”，乐师说“倚靠把梯子靠在墙上这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 leaning the ladder against the wall 作主语。
lean 意为“倾斜”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去倾斜风暴过后歪向一边”，should ever 之后用原形 lean to one side after the storm。
lean 意为“倾斜”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻倾斜风暴过后歪向一边（lean to one side after the storm at once），以后再也不要提起。
lean 意为“倚靠”，新来的听客每个夜晚都照例倾斜风暴过后歪向一边，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 leans。
lean 意为“倚靠”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次天没亮就倚靠把梯子靠在墙上，用一般过去式 leaned 叙述。
lean 意为“倚靠”，结尾那句是母亲 2000 年的话：要倚靠把梯子靠在墙上，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和音乐厅记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 lean 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1988 the musician leaned the ladder against the wall before dawn, and nobody in the hall forgot it.
Even now the musician leans the ladder against the wall in public whenever the hall asks.
Leaning the ladder against the wall before dawn, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever lean to one side after the storm in public, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new listener from the next hall leans to one side after the storm before dawn every night, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother leaned the ladder against the wall again, and the hall remembered that half.
